candidate_claims.statement: The blog post is titled 'Music of Our Childhood'.
The blog post lists 'Publicado por Julia' as the author.
María Elena Walsh has put music into the childhood of every Argentine since the late Sixties.
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: María Elena Walsh has put music into the childhood of every Argentine since the late Sixties.

candidate_claims.statement: The post's author states that she thinks María Elena Walsh's work was a true revolution regarding the way of talking to children, the way of singing to them and of telling them stories.
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: I think that hers was a true revolution regarding the way of talking to children, the way of singing to them and of telling them stories.

candidate_claims.statement: According to the post, María Elena Walsh never used the silly, didactic manner of a narrow-minded school teacher.
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: Never did she use the silly, didactic manner of a narrow-minded school teacher.

candidate_claims.statement: The post says 'Manuelita, la tortuga' is perhaps María Elena Walsh's most famous song for children.
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: "Manuelita, la tortuga" is perhaps her most famous song for children.

candidate_claims.statement: The lyrics of the songs and the text of the whole post have been translated from Spanish to English by María Lía Macchi.
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: (The lyrics of the songs and the text of the whole post have been translated from Spanish to English by María Lía Macchi. Once again, thanks for the great job!)

candidate_claims.statement: The song lyrics include the line 'Manuelita vivía en Pehuajó pero un día se marchó.'
candidate_claims.supporting_excerpt: Manuelita vivía en Pehuajó pero un día se marchó.
